title: An overlapped copy engine
hints: Keep the operations in flight in a map from id to operation: a completion only carries the id, and you need the offset and length back to decide what comes next.

Write one helper that starts reads while chunks remain and the limit allows, and call it from `start` and after every completed write; a completed read is simply replaced by its write, so it never changes the count.
Decide the order of checks for a completion carefully: unknown id first, then "is this an error", then "have we already failed or been cancelled", and only then the normal read and write handling.
requirements: Chunks cover the file exactly, with the right last-chunk length, and an empty file is finished at once.
The in-flight limit is never exceeded, and the pipeline stays full while there is work.
Every read is followed by a write of the same bytes at the same offset, whatever order completions arrive in.
Short or long reads and errors fail the copy with the right code; after failure or cancellation nothing new starts.
Cancellation returns exactly the operations in flight, and aborted completions after it are not failures.
